evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Key terms (game, name, optional description) have a single reasonable interpretation in this context.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting via a game access URL is clear and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: The action and input mechanism are specific enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: "See all items" is ambiguous about scope (planned vs actually estimated vs including deleted/re-estimated items) and what constitutes an "item" view, allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item for (re-)estimation is clear given the established concept of items/rounds in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list is a straightforward operation with no materially different interpretations implied.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: "Edit an item" is underspecified: it could mean editing only the text, also the estimate, ordering, metadata, or history; these are materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: "Delete" can mean remove from the session list, soft-delete with audit/history, or delete including associated estimates; these are materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: "Immediately" is vague (timing/trigger) and "show all estimates" could mean reveal current-round estimates only vs including prior rounds; materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: "Average" is ambiguous (mean vs median vs rounded mean; handling of non-numeric/special cards) leading to materially different calculations.

evaluations.evidence: if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous trigger conditions: does it require all invited, all joined, or all currently participating estimators; and what counts as "same card" if decks differ/contain special cards.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering a final estimate is clear; the agreement process is outside the story and does not create multiple interpretations of the required function.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether re-estimation creates a new round entry, overwrites the prior estimate, or keeps multiple estimates per story; materially different data/UX outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: "Spreadsheet" and "import" are underspecified (file types, required columns/format, mapping rules), enabling materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous input format and parsing rules (rows/columns, delimiters, multi-line cells), leading to materially different behavior.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: "Browse" is vague (search, filter, pagination, sorting) and "previous games" scope is unclear (owned by user vs all games), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: "Transcript" is an abstraction that could include different contents (chat, timestamps, participants, per-round details) beyond "stories and estimates"; materially different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Depends on ambiguous "transcript" content and also unclear HTML structure/packaging (single file vs assets), enabling materially different exports.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV schema is unspecified (columns, row granularity per story/round/estimate), leading to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: "Delete" could mean hard delete vs soft delete/archival; "no longer stored" could mean not accessible vs physically removed—materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Required fields are explicitly listed and the action is clear.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: "Account name" is ambiguous relative to PP-021 which distinguishes email address and username; could mean either, leading to different login identifiers.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: "Account details" is vague (which fields: name/email/username/password?) and may imply different permissions/flows.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: "Delete"/"no longer stored" is ambiguous (hard delete vs deactivation; treatment of games/shared data), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: "Local timezone" is ambiguous (browser-detected vs profile setting) and scope of which dates/times is unspecified, leading to different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: "Password reminder" is ambiguous (send existing password vs reset link/token), which are materially different security/functional behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Two concrete card sets are specified, making the choice clear despite the illustrative "etc.".

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: The limit and action are explicit and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL and entering a name is clear enough for a single interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: The item being estimated is a well-established concept in the backlog and the requirement is straightforward.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: "Will try to estimate" is ambiguous about inclusion (added later, deleted, already estimated, re-estimated), allowing materially different lists.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: "Immediately" is vague (real-time push vs polling/refresh) and "see that an estimate has been given" could mean reveal value vs only indicate submitted; materially different behavior.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: The reveal condition (after all estimators have estimated) and simultaneous display are clear in intent.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: "Last person" is ambiguous (last among invited vs joined vs active) and the exact completion event is unclear, leading to different cutoff rules.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: "Prior estimates" is ambiguous (earlier rounds in same game vs across games; includes re-estimates?) causing materially different data scope.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Scope is constrained to the current round and the mapping of estimator to estimate is clear.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous who can start it (any participant vs specific roles) and whether multiple timers/overrides are allowed; materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: "We all" is ambiguous (all invited/joined/active estimators) and "play an estimate" event definition is unclear, leading to different reset triggers.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: "Scroll back" is vague about UI/extent and "prior rounds" could mean within current game only vs across games; materially different scope.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: "Same order" is ambiguous (fixed canonical order vs user-defined; per deck type) and "draws" could mean rounds within a game vs across games/sessions.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: "Draw" and "completed" are not defined and could map to different lifecycle events (all submitted vs revealed vs accepted), yielding different cutoffs.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: "Near" and "where my cards are played" are vague UI references that allow materially different placements and behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: "Compliant" and which specific versions/levels of XHTML/CSS are intended are unclear, enabling materially different interpretations of the requirement.

evaluations.evidence: a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: "Commonly used terms" is vague (which terms, where sourced, completeness), allowing materially different scopes for the glossary.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Which tables/columns/queries require indexes is unspecified; could lead to materially different indexing strategies and outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: "Function correctly" is vague (which features, acceptable degradation, rendering vs behavior), allowing materially different interpretations of compatibility.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: "Where possible" is inherently ambiguous and the specific guideline/version/level is not stated, enabling materially different compliance targets.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: "Quickly" is subjective and allows materially different performance requirements (e.g., 200ms vs 2s).

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: "Use Unicode" is underspecified (input only vs storage vs display; which fields; normalization), leading to materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: "Sensible" and "predictable" are subjective and can be interpreted in materially different URL design schemes.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: "Nice" and "something goes wrong" are vague, allowing materially different requirements for styling, content, and error coverage.

evaluations.evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: "Non-identifiable" is ambiguous (pseudonymized vs anonymized; what identifiers; re-identification risk threshold), leading to materially different data handling requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: "Some metrics" is vague (which metrics, time range, granularity), enabling materially different interpretations of what must be provided.
